business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Retailing of Fast-Fashion Apparel and Footwear

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 52 de 2016 (Uniformly applicable to bearer shares and creation of the Beneficial Ownership Registry), amended by Ley 129 de 2020; Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (AML/CFT framework); Executive Decree No. 789 de 2022 (Regulatory provisions for the Beneficial Ownership Registry attached to the Panama Public Registry); Resolution No. 2020-04 of the Superintendencia de Sujetos No Financieros (SSNF); CDD Guidelines of the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of Valid Passport of each Director, Officer, Shareholder and Ultimate Beneficial Owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public or Consulate of Panama in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for Incorporation and Representation before the Panama Public Registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Corporate Existence from the Parent or Legal Entity Registry (if the shareholder is a legal entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cogent Registry or Companies House in the jurisdiction of the parent entity

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified List of Officers, Directors and Shareholders (Acta / Certificación de Accionistas) for the Ultimate Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the parent company's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if the origin jurisdiction is not an Apostille member

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All proposed directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, registered agents, and significant commercial counterparties must undergo mandatory and continuous screening against the Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) database, the United States OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the European Union Consolidated Sanctions List, and the domestic Consolidated List maintained by the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF). Negative news and adverse media screening is mandatory. Where any PEP is identified as a shareholder or director, enhanced due diligence (EDD), source of funds evidence, and senior managerial approval are required prior to incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único de Nombre Comercial (RUNC) / Online Name Reservation Portal of the Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be submitted in the Spanish language; limited Latin-script transliteration is permitted for foreign brand names. The name must consist of at least one distinguishing word plus a corporate suffix such as 'S.A.', 'Corp.', or 'Inc.' The proposed name must be phonetically and visually distinguishable from existing registered names within the Panama Public Registry and must not violate third party trademarks or trade names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name is rejected, the applicant or its licensed registered agent must file a written reconsideración (administrative appeal) within five (5) business days after the date of rejection with the Name Clearance Division (Dirección de Registro) of the Panama Public Registry. The appeal must attach prior trademark search results, consent letters from the conflicting name holder, or evidence of distinctiveness. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file an apelación en subsidio before the General Directorate (Dirección General) of the Panama Public Registry within ten (10) business days. An adverse final administrative decision may be challenged before the Third Chamber of the Supreme Court of Justice (Corte Suprema de Justicia) within two (2) months.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are permissible for the initial pre-operational phase of a fast-fashion e-commerce business (ISIC 4791). However, Panama law requires every Sociedad Anónima registered in the country to maintain a physical registered office address in Panama managed by a licensed registered agent. A virtual address provided by a licensed registered agent is acceptable to the Public Registry, but the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) may disregard the virtual address if the company applies for an Import License, VAT registration, or executes recurring e-commerce transactions, and may require evidence of real commercial substance (i.e., lease agreement, dedicated personnel, warehouse or third-party fulfillment contract).
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (10%) for non-regulated e-commerce (ISIC 4791) at the initial incorporation stage; however, DGI conducts unannounced inspections of digital retailers that register for VAT and fail to remit consumer taxes collected. If any director or UBO is a PEP, the risk rises to a Moderate (30%) likelihood of supervision by the UAF or an on-site verification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 32 de 1927 (General Corporation Law of the Republic of Panama), as amended and consolidated; relevant provisions: Articles 1–13 (formation and incorporation), Articles 14–26 (capital, shares and subscriptions), Articles 27–49 (directors, officers and corporate governance), and Article 28 (reserved powers of the board).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Departamento de Registro Mercantil y de Personas Jurídicas (Public Registry of Panama, Mercantile and Legal Persons Registration Department), Panama City.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public Deed of Incorporation of a Corporation — 'Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad Anónima' (containing the Pacto Social y Estatutos), presented for inscription in the Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement under Law 32 of 1927. The S.A. must subscribe and issue at least one (1) share; the incorporators declare the subscribed capital in the deed for statutory and stamp-tax purposes, and full payment may be deferred as provided in the Articles.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY], S.A. 1. The subscription and issuance of the initial authorized shares, as recorded in the Share Register, are hereby ratified; no minimum paid-up capital is required under Law 32 of 1927. 2. The registered office is fixed at the offices of the Resident Agent, [full address], Panama City, Republic of Panama. 3. [President Name] is appointed President, [Secretary Name] Secretary, and [Treasurer Name] Treasurer, each with the powers conferred by the corporate Statutes. 4. The Resident Agent is authorized to file this resolution and to complete all Public Registry registrations. Adopted this [day] of [month], 20[year].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Oficina de Reserva de Nombre (Name Reservation Office), Panama City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the digital 'Solicitud de Reserva de Nombre' through the Registro Público online platform (SIRP) or at the name-reservation window, submitting up to three proposed corporate names in descending order of preference. Pay the search/reservation fee and obtain the Certificado de Reserva de Nombre, which is valid for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Solicitud de Reserva de Nombre (application form)
Copy of applicant's passport or cédula
Power of attorney (Poder) if filed by an attorney-in-fact
Payment receipt of the name-search fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused as identical or confusingly similar to a prior registration, promptly file a new reservation using an alternate name; the rejected name itself cannot be cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Deed of Incorporation Before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the Judicial Circuit (Notaría del Circuito de Panamá), acting through the licensed incorporating attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporating attorney (Resident Agent) drafts the Articles of Incorporation and convenes at least two incorporators or their attorneys-in-fact to execute the deed before a Panamanian notary. The deed must state the corporate name, domicile, plural corporate purpose, capital structure (subscribed and paid-in), indefinite term, number of directors, and the board's powers under Article 28 of Law 32 of 1927. The notary certifies signatures and issues the Testimonio.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Reserva de Nombre
Draft of the Pacto Social y Estatutos
Passport/cédula copies of incorporators and the three initial directors
Power of attorney (Poder) granted to the incorporating attorney
Written acceptance of the Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If statutory gaps are detected, the deed is reformed and re-executed in the same notarial act before registration; minor recitals are corrected by a marginal note ('nota de nota') at no additional notarial charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Fiscal Stamps and Initial Registry Presentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Tesorería y Ventanilla de Recepción (Cashier and Document Reception Office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the registry inscription fees and stamp duties at the Registro Público cashier using the assessment generated by the SIRP system. Submit the original testimonio together with the fee receipts; the Registry assigns a received-file number and queues the dossier for legal examination.
required_dossiers: Original notarized Testimonio de la Escritura
Certificado de Reserva de Nombre
Registry fee payment receipts
Copy of the attorney's or incorporator's tax identification (RUC) if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of a fee dispute or defective docketing, obtain a corrected assessment from the Tesorería and re-submit the same day; missing stamps are cured by supplemental payment before examination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription and Issuance of Legal Capacity Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Dirección de Registro (Mercantil) / Registro de Personas Jurídicas
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The examining registrar verifies legality and records the inscription note ('nota de inscripción') at the margin of the deed. Following inscription, request the Certificado de Personería Jurídica and certified copies of the registered deed; the corporation acquires legal personality as of the date of the deed.
required_dossiers: Testimonio de la Escritura as filed
Solicitud de Inscripción (inscription application)
Any correction orders issued by the registrar (defecto)
Payment receipt for the personería certificate stamp
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a 'defecto' (deficiency), the attorney must cure within five business days by supplementing documents or amending the deed as ordered; an unsatisfied suspension may be appealed to the Directora General del Registro Público within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Fiscal and Commercial Activation (RUC and Municipal Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Registro Único de Contribuyentes; Municipio de Panamá — Dirección de Rentas Municipales
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation with the DGI to obtain the RUC, confirming territorial tax status and monthly ITBMS obligations. Then file the Aviso de Operación with the Municipality of Panama for the declared activity code ISIC 4791, pay the proportional municipal tax, and obtain the municipal operating permit after the inspection visit.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Personería Jurídica
Certified copy of the inscribed deed and by-laws
Identity documents of directors and officers
RUC application form (DGI forms 102/105 equivalents)
Municipal Aviso de Operación application and fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI or Municipality disputes the activity classification, correct the declared code to ISIC 4791 and pay any proportional municipal rate; delayed RUC responses are expedited by written request at the DGI ventanilla única attaching the personería certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 4791 electronic retailing of fast-fashion apparel is a non-industrial activity; no manufacturing concession or industrial license is required from the Dirección General de Industrias, Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating permit required. Applicable operational clearances are the municipal Aviso de Operación and the DGI/RUC tax registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I (registration/exempt) under Law No. 41 of 1998 (Ley General del Ambiente) and MiAMBIENTE category rules; a full EIA Report is not required for e-commerce retailing or light warehousing of packaged apparel.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process-related discharges for pure apparel retail. General procedural thresholds apply under the national wastewater-discharge regulation: pH 6–9, BOD5 ≤ 250 mg/L, TSS ≤ 250 mg/L before any municipal sewer connection; no volatile-organic-compound emission source; solid waste must be handled by licensed haulers and textile waste recycled where municipal collection is available.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá fire-safety certificate for offices and storage areas (NFPA-compliant detectors and extinguishers); municipal engineering structural/inspection clearance for any physical premises used by the e-commerce retailer; and, where staff exceed 10 employees, workplace hygiene registration with the Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), dependent organ of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); official e-filing portal: 'Sede Electrónica' at https://dgi.mef.gob.pa (and https://www.dgi.gob.pa). The DGI administers the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC), the ITBMS, income tax (ISR), the simplified SME regime, and electronic invoicing authorization.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Incorporate the Sociedad Anónima (S.A.) at the Registro Público de Panamá through a licensed agent with a resident agent and registered officers (Canon corporate annuity paid). Step 2 — Obtain municipal 'Aviso de Operación' (Comercio/licencia) at the appropriate Municipio for the commercial address. Step 3 — Register with the DGI's Sede Electrónica using the incorporated company's notarial documents, municipal license, and a Firma Electrónica Calificada (digital certificate issued by a certified authority); DGI issues the RUC for the Panamanian branch/S.A. including the indicative tax classification (Territorial ITBMS, employer at PAYEE). Step 4 — If gross taxable income exceeds B/.36,000 per year (or voluntarily), file the ITBMS registration form (Formulario 111/Inscripción ITBMS) at the DGI with proof of bank account and local legal representation. Step 5 — Register for the electronic invoicing system (DGI-FEL) selecting the free 'Facturador Web' or a certified billing software, and obtain the activation codes and digital stamp. Foreign non-resident principals must act through the resident agent and provide certified incorporation certificates, passport/legal entity documents, and AML/KYC file (Law 23 of 2015).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope — A Panamanian S.A. is taxed at the entity level solely on Panama-source income; foreign-source income (including foreign e-commerce retail sales) is outside the taxable base and no remittance tax applies. Panamanian inside-Panama B2C sales of fast-fashion apparel are attributed to Panama and subject to income tax (25% standard ISR; effective progressive rate for the regulated small/medium business) plus ITBMS on the gross sale. The entity is not a pass-through; dividends distributed from already-taxed Panama-source profits attract a 5% dividend tax (when paid to residents) or 10% (to non-residents), while undistributed foreign-source profit remains exempt. No economic-substance minimum is required by law, but DGI may attribute offshore activity where administrative, decision-making, and invoicing functions are actually performed from Panama; the 'Tax Exempt Zone' classification is unavailable except where the company elects the Colón Free Zone or SEM regime for qualifying service hubs, which does not apply to this fast-fashion e-commerce scope.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not adopt US 'check-the-box' or hybrid-mismatch elections; the S.A. is a taxable corporation by default. Available elections/regimes: (i) voluntary ITBMS registration for taxpayers below the B/.36,000 gross-turnover threshold; (ii) election to be taxed under the 'Régimen Simplificado de Tributación' (RST, simplified method) for small retailers with annual gross income under B/.200,000 and payroll parameters, where income tax is replaced by a 2% (gross) ITBMS-equivalent advance, reducing bookkeeping burden; (iii) election between territorial versus non-territorial treatment is not available, but a taxpayer can choose branch (permanent establishment) versus subsidiary structure for foreign expansion; (iv) election to apply the 'Sede de Empresa Multinacional' (SEM) benefits (5% royalty/Dividend treatment, ITBMS exemption on imported services) requires a separate license from the SEM Commission and is not applicable to mere apparel merchandising; (v) option to request the 'Régimen de Tributación Internacional (RIT)'? — no; fiscal consolidation is not elective. DGI prior filing is required for any election to change the taxable year or to obtain an advanced-pricing agreement.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (value-added tax integrated into Arts. 1057–1087 of the Código Fiscal and the 2010 Ley 8 regime). Panama applies a territorial consumption tax to all transfers of movable goods, service provisions, and imports consumed or used in Panamanian territory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/.36,000 (equivalent to USD 36,000) of gross taxable income per calendar year in Panama; mandatory ITBMS registration and monthly/ bimonthly returns above this threshold; registration below the threshold is voluntary but advisable to recover input credits. E-commerce and cross-border digital retail of apparel is within the taxable subject matter: each delivery of goods physically in Panama triggers ITBMS at 7% (plus 10% for alcohol/tabacco/hotels, which does not impact fashion apparel).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory since September 2023 for all ITBMS-registered taxpayers. Issuance rules: (i) invoices must be generated through DGI-FEL (Facturación Electrónica en Línea) using either DGI's free 'Facturador' web tool or certified ERP/POS software integrated by APIs in XML/JSON; (ii) each invoice must contain a unique consecutive number, QR code, tax classification code, the RUC-N point of sale, and an authorization number/ 'Sello Digital' issued by DGI in near-real time; (iii) Panama's system is 'pre-issued authorization' — the invoice must be transmitted to DGI's platform before issuance to obtain the cufe-like authorization code (not a continuous real-time clearance as in Mexico, but an online pre-issuance control with 24-hour transmission windows for retailers); (iv) the free DGI portal is available to small filers without API costs; no additional plataforma of 'retención' applies at the B2C level for payment gateways (Klarna BNPL / Shopify Payments) unless the gateway is a Panamanian financial institution subject to withholding; (v) fiscal point-of-sale (digital fiscal equipment) is no longer mandatory for purely online sellers; the electronic receipt is sufficient; (vi) penalties for non-issuance: surcharge of 10% of the invoice, fine, and possible suspension of the RUC within the DGI registry.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: Exports of tangible merchandise from Panama are zero-rated (0% ITBMS) where (i) the seller holds legal title, (ii) the merchandise physically departs Panama under a valid customs export process, (iii) the final delivery address is outside Panama and the sale is to a non-resident purchaser (export evidence: DUEX + B/L + payment from abroad), and (iv) the sale is made and invoiced by the Panamanian company. Services: services qualify as 'exportados' when the beneficiary is a non-resident (or a SEM/ multinational head office abroad), the benefit/use occurs outside Panama, and the consideration enters Panama's banking system; offshore-targeted logistics, fulfillment, marketing and marketplace-support services bundled with fast-fashion e-commerce can be zero-rated if supported by a service agreement showing foreign use. Critical caveats: sales delivered to a Panama address (local warehouse/ P.O. box) are always taxed at 7%, even if the payment gateway is foreign; returns are subject to ITBMS reversal rules where the original invoice was zero-rated — the refund credit requires a negative export invoice. Input tax credits (ITBMS paid on local purchases of inventory? — inventory imports, logistics, packaging, and marketplace fees) are recoverable under the exporter's 'crédito fiscal' regime; a refund ('devolución de ITBMS') is claimable quarterly, however DGI practice requires offset against other taxes first and physical audited verification.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Declaración Única de Exportación (DUEX) — customs export declaration issued by the Ministerio de Comercio/ Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas evidencing ISIC-compatible apparel/footwear exit from Panama
Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill — transport document showing the port/airport of exit and foreign delivery point
Commercial invoice marked 'EXPORTACIÓN / 0% ITBMS' with item-level description of fast-fashion SKUs, Incoterms, and foreign buyer VAT number

Inward Remittance Certificate / bank statement — credit advice from Banco Nacional de Panamá or a licensed bank evidencing the proceeds received from the foreign customer within the Panamanian banking system (proceeds may be received in USD with no exchange requirement due to the Balboa/USD peg)
Proof of foreign destination — online order details, shipping manifest from the e-commerce platform and logistics contract (for Shopify / Klarna / marketplace receipts)
Certificate of Origin (optional yet recommended) and the customs 'Formulario de Movimiento' where goods move through a zona franca
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI audits zero-rating claims with a documentary chain-of-evidence requirement; missing B/L or payment credit triggers automatic recharacterization of the invoice as a domestic taxable sale, with retrospective assessment of 7% ITBMS plus interest. Clawback window: the DGI may review and claw back input credits and zero-rating benefits within a 5-year limitation period (Art. 790 Código Fiscal), extended to 8 years where no return was filed or where the taxpayer intentionally concealed documents (Art. 790 As amended by Ley 8 de 2010). Penalties: (i) surcharge of 10% per annum on the unpaid ITBMS (Art. 741); (ii) fines of B/.50 to B/.10,000 plus a 20% increase of the omitted tax when forms were incorrectly filed; (iii) for simulated export operations / fraud, the 'delito fiscal' offense under Art. 792-H carries imprisonment of 3 to 5 years, increased to 5 to 10 years where the evaded amount exceeds B/.100,000; (iv) civil liability of the S.A. directors and the resident agent for knowingly issuing false export documents, under the Código Fiscal and Law 23 AML-restrictions; (v) denial of the export refund and mandatory registration in the DGI defaulters list, blocking the RUC and customs clearance. In practice, the DGI also cross-checks freight-forwarder manifests, Amazon/eBay/Shopify payment reports, and credit-card acquirer records from Klarna/Shopify Payments to flag mismatches between declared export destinations and physical delivery addresses.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no central bank. Banking supervision rests with the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá; Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent and clearing agent; due to full dollarization, monetary policy is effectively set by the U.S. Federal Reserve.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility. The Panamanian balboa is a token currency pegged 1:1 to the U.S. dollar, and the U.S. dollar is legal tender. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible without prior Central Bank authorization or reporting. Profit remittance is unrestricted; dividends derived from Panama-source income are subject to a 10% withholding tax after effect? place. There are no exchange controls, no surrender requirements, and no restrictions on holding foreign currency.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory obligation to repatriate, deposit locally, convert, or surrender export proceeds. Exporters may retain and use proceeds in USD or any convertible currency, whether onshore or offshore.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate. Panama allows payment-service providers and e-money institutions to operate only under a license from the Superintendencia de Bancos or as regulated fintech companies under Law 147 of 2021 and related rules. Offshore EMIs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Revolut) are not locally chartered and cannot issue Panamanian local clearing accounts or local IBANs (Panama uses no IBAN standard). They are viable only as auxiliary payment aggregators or inbound/outbound remittance rails, not as primary treasury clearing institutions for a Panamanian S.A.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Generally required. Tier-1 Panamanian banks mandate an in-person interview at a local branch for the legal representative and/or beneficial owner(s) of a Sociedad Anónima, with original passports, notarized and apostilled corporate by-laws and articles, and a certificate of incumbency. Remote opening is possible only for existing high-value clients with a private-bank relationship, and even then a video conference and independent local counsel attestation are the practical minimum.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity when the S.A. is owned through bearer shares or a foundation without full disclosure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly notarized and apostilled UBO chain documentation, current registry certificate (Registro Público de Panamá) showing directors and residents agent, legalized by-laws, sworn declaration of beneficial ownership, and valid passports of all natural persons above 10% ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High cross-border transaction volume to/from fast-fashion e-commerce in multiple jurisdictions without a physical office in Panama
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Leased office agreement in Panama, corporate website with physical address, commercial contracts with suppliers/inventory, invoices, shipment tracking documentation, Shopify panel statements, and a business plan explaining the territorial nexus to Panama.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of third-party payment processors (Shopify Payments, Klarna BNPL) causing KYC mismatch between bank-account holder and recorded payee
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Binding payment-processor agreements showing the S.A. as the contracting legal entity, reconciliation statements mapping all processor settlements to the corporate bank account, and a signed legal opinion or affidavit stating that processor remittances represent settlement of the company's own receivables.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions with flash-trade suppliers or invoicing from high-risk apparel wholesaler jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade invoices, Bills of Lading or airway bills, import customs declarations, supplier KYC packages, known-customer background checks, and a coherent funds-flow narrative for each significant payment request.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from parent/shareholder entities should be remitted via SWIFT MT103 from a bank in the remitter's own jurisdiction. The beneficiary account must match the S.A.'s full corporate name and local PayPal? Use purpose code 3010 (equity capital) for shareholder loans or direct investment, or 9009 (other intercompany transactions) where appropriate. For Panamanian banks, the remittance must include an instruction referencing the capital-escrow account or operational account and, if above USD 10,000, a KYC form identifying the final beneficiary and source of funds. Physical or virtual escrow closing may require a notarized capital-injection agreement and board resolution.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for fast-fashion inventory purchases should clear through SWIFT MT103 for low-to-mid value payments, and Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) at sight or with 60-90 day usance for higher-value structured supplier transactions. The primary clearing rails are the U.S. banking network (Fedwire/CHIPS) clearing USD efficiently through Panamanian correspondent banks. For BNPL and consumer payment arrangements with Shopify Payments, aggregate proceeds are settled to the corporate bank account via daily or weekly ACH or SWIFT in USD. Export receipts can remain in USD in offshore correspondent accounts without mandatory conversion.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forwards against USD/EUR, USD/CNH, USD/GBP for known payables and receivables schedules
Cross-currency swaps (USD/CAD, USD/MXN) for longer-dated liability hedging
Vanilla FX options to hedge non-USD exposure generated by third-party processors

Because the functional currency is the U.S. dollar and Panama has no domestic exchange control, non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are unnecessary in the Panamanian legal environment but may be accessed from global banks for administratively convenient hedging of non-convertible supplier-side currencies only.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Payment of Annual Franchise Tax (Tasa Única Anual) applicable to every Sociedad Anónima
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Panama Ministry of Economy and Finance; payment submitted through the registered agent using the DGI taxpayer account
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 15 January of each calendar year; newly incorporated companies cover the first year at incorporation and begin the annual cycle in the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of USD 110 per year; failure to pay for three consecutive years triggers administrative dissolution and strike-off at Registro Público; continued delinquency prevents issuance of certificates of good standing and may expose directors and the resident agent to fines

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (Declaración Anual de Beneficiario Final) under Law 70 of 2019
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Beneficial Ownership Registry (Directorio de Transparencia y Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March; any shareholding or beneficial ownership change must additionally be reported within 30 business days after the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to USD 5,000 for late, false, or omitted declarations; repeated violations may suspend corporate rights and restrict access to public registry certificates

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory external audit for ordinary private Sociedades Anónimas without a Panama business license (Aviso de Operación). Compulsory audit applies to regulated entities (banks, insurers, securities issuers) and to Panama operational license holders with annual gross income exceeding USD 3,000,000 or total assets exceeding USD 5,000,000 under DGI large-taxpayer rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama for publicly held and regulated entities; Local GAAP acceptable for private companies not subject to SMV or banking supervision. Accounting records must support the territorial-source income tax return and be prepared on an accrual basis.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The resident agent or DGI-designated filer must confirm the full ownership chain and beneficial ownership status each year before 31 March. Every share transfer requires endorsement in the corporate share ledger, notarization where required, and an updated UBO declaration to DGI within 30 business days. The annual confirmation is separate from day-to-day register updating; the Register of Members must be maintained continuously and not merely on an annual basis.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Corporate Resolutions and Minute Book (Libro de Actas y Resoluciones)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 - USD 700 per year for resident-agent services including registered office, franchise tax filing, and UBO submission
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 5,000 per year when an audit is triggered; private companies generally incur only bookkeeping or outside accounting fees of USD 600 - USD 2,500

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday or preferential deduction for fast-fashion e-commerce; the territorial system excludes foreign-source income, so only Panama-source internet sales bear the effective 25% rate, reduced by ordinary deductions (COGS, logistics, platform and payment-processing fees).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1522 (annual income tax return) filed through SITIO, the DGI online portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than 3 months after fiscal year-end (31 March for calendar-year taxpayers; non-calendar FYEs require prior DGI authorization).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification number (Registro Único de Contribuyente).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be the permanent RUC of the Panama S.A.; provisional numbers cannot be used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross e-commerce receipts from fast-fashion apparel sold to Panama-domiciled consumers, net of returns and allowances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the territorial source rule: only income linked to Panama is reportable; foreign online sales are excluded from the base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, fulfillment, last-mile delivery, marketing, transaction fees, and IT costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Support with proper invoices; cross-border recharge from group entities must respect the arm's-length standard even when below TP filing thresholds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 17 (Net taxable base and tax payable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after NOL deductions, multiplied by 25%, less monthly advance credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the Form 1530 advances; overpayments are creditable or refundable.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-filing surcharge of 10% of the tax due plus 1% monthly delinquency interest; non-filing allows DGI presumptive assessment and can trigger criminal tax-fraud prosecution under Law 70 of 2019.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1530 (monthly estimated CIT and ITBMS declaration) filed through SITIO.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before the 15th day of the following calendar month.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Coefficient-based monthly installment equal to 1/12 of the prior fiscal year's income tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: First-year S.A. files at zero until the initial Form 1522 creates a coefficient; monthly wire traces must be retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 7% transfer tax collected on local taxable sales of apparel and footwear.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 7% applies to goods delivered in Panama even if the seller is a foreign digital storefront; treaty/exemption certificates must be pre-validated.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Unpaid amounts accrue 1% monthly interest plus a 10% surcharge; habitual omission is treated as badges of fraud in criminal tax proceedings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1523 (annual transfer-pricing informative declaration) filed through SITIO.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on or before 30 June following the fiscal year-end (six months after FYE for non-calendar-year taxpayers).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identification of all related parties with intercompany dealings, including the foreign parent and group finance companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all group entities even where no payment was made; the indicator is the existence of controlled transactions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section C (Transaction values and TP method)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Value of each related-party transaction category and the pricing method selected.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select the most reliable method for the fast-fashion chain; typically TNMM for logistics/fulfillment recharges and CUP for platform resale margins.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Daily fine of B/. 100 until filed, plus upward TP adjustment of the taxable base, 1% monthly interest and 10% surcharge on understated tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% final dividend withholding on profits that have borne the 25% CIT; distributions sourced from untaxed profits (tax-loss years or in excess of the year's taxable base) are subject to a 10% dividend tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial-owner shareholder must supply the Panamanian paying entity, before the dividend is paid, with (i) a valid Tax Residence Certificate issued by the treaty country tax authority, (ii) a completed DGI treaty-relief form certifying beneficial ownership and non-residence in Panama, and (iii) proof of entitlement under the applicable DTA (typically 5% to 15% dividend rate). The payer files the reduced-rate withholding through SITIO and retains the documentation for at least five years; no prior DGI ruling is required.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on gross royalties and technical-assistance fees paid to non-residents: 12.5%; interest on Panama-source loans paid to non-resident lenders: 12.5%, unless the payee is an accredited bank or the obligation is a registered public offering (0%). DTA protocols typically lower interest to 2%-10% and royalties to 5%-12.5% on certification of beneficial ownership.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/. 250,000 in aggregate related-party transactions per fiscal year triggers the mandatory Form 1523 filing; Local File and Master File documentation must be prepared when annual consolidated gross revenue exceeds B/. 3,000,000 or affected transactions exceed B/. 1,000,000, and must be submitted within 45 days of a DGI request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's ESR (Law 254 of 2019), in force since FY 2019, subject S.A.s to substance requirements where they perform relevant activities, inclusive of distribution and service centers and IP-bearing operations. The fast-fashion e-commerce S.A. must demonstrate local management and execution of core income-generating activities—inventory procurement, logistics chain governance, pricing, and treasury decisions—through a physical office, resident officers and proportionate local spend; failure exposes the entity to ESR fines, loss of tax-residence certification and denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of Panama-source e-commerce revenue, diversion of sales to a related offshore entity without economic substance, or failure to file Form 1522 in order to suppress the 25% CIT liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud under Law 70 of 2019: 3 to 5 years' imprisonment for simple evasion and 5 to 10 years for aggravated evasion using sham structures and false records, together with a fine equal to 100% of the evaded tax, closure of the commercial establishment and revocation of the business license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners who directed the concealment are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, interest and fine; criminal courts may impose travel bans, asset freezing, and disqualification from corporate management during the proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and inadequate economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the S.A. as a hollow booking vehicle—no Panamanian office, employees or management substance—while booking group e-commerce profits in Panama or invoking DTA relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESR administrative fines, forced deregistration of the corporate license, DGI denial of tax-residence certificates, and recharacterization of the income as taxable at 25% with the further 10% dividend complement on deemed distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Resident agents and directors who certify false substance filings are personally fined and may be prosecuted for falsifying corporate books; intentional evasion through a shell entity aggravates criminal exposure up to the maximum fraud sanction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-money laundering and beneficial ownership breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to keep the mandatory beneficial-ownership register, issuance of bearer shares without immobilization, or accepting payment flows without applying risk-based due diligence to Klarna BNPL or Shopify Pay transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML administrative fines under Law 23 of 2015 scaled by subject category (up to B/. 1,000,000 for regulated entities); money-laundering prosecution carries imprisonment of 5 to 12 years, extendable in aggravated cases, plus confiscation of proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false beneficial-ownership declarations face personal criminal prosecution, travel bans, seizure of personal and corporate assets, and disqualification from serving on Panamanian boards.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting Form 1523 despite group-related purchase volumes above B/. 250,000, or refusing to supply Local/Master File documentation within the 45-day statutory window on DGI request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Daily penalty of B/. 100 for non-filing plus upward adjustment of the taxable base, 1% monthly interest and a 10% surcharge on the understated CIT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Management approving non-arm's-length intercompany prices is jointly assessed for the underpaid tax and may be barred from filing tax declarations for any Panamanian entity for a period fixed by the DGI.
